Items.itemDescription: A staple crop that sustains both man and beast. It can be ground into flour for bread or brewed into ale.
Rich and hearty, this meat is prized for its flavor and nourishment, especially during harsh winters.
A thick, warm pelt from a wild deer, perfect for crafting garments or trading with those in need of protection from the cold.
Soft and light, this fur is often used in crafting light garments or as a base for fine leatherworking.
A sturdy, heavy material, essential for forging weapons and armor that can withstand even the fiercest of battles.
A reddish metal, prized for its use in creating tools and ornaments. It’s not as strong as iron, but still valuable.
A pale metal that, when combined with copper, forms bronze—a key material in the crafting of weapons and armor.
Precious stones that gleam with a rare beauty. These are highly sought after by traders, jewelers, and mages alike.
A rich, fermented drink brewed from barley and hops. It brings warmth to the weary and mirth to the men around the fire.
A honeyed drink brewed by bees, prized by many for its sweet taste and mild intoxication. It’s a favorite among bards and warriors alike.
A soft and insulating fiber, sheared from the sheep, it is spun into threads to make warm garments for cold nights.
Tender and flavorful, lamb meat is considered a delicacy among many, often cooked over an open flame to bring out its rich taste.
A fine cloth made from flax, valued for its breathability and smooth texture. Often used for making light, summer garments.
Sweet, golden nectar harvested from the hives. It’s used both as a food and for its medicinal properties, especially in healing salves.
A natural wax produced by bees, used for sealing, crafting, and even for lighting lamps. It’s versatile and valuable in many forms.
A sturdy blade forged from iron. Reliable in any skirmish.
Cured meat that lasts long and travels well. A favorite among caravaners.
A warm, simple tunic made from thick wool. Keeps the cold out.
A simple candle made from tallow. Provides basic light for several hours.
Ground grain ready for baking or trade. A staple for any kitchen.
Lamb meat grilled to perfection, served hot and juicy. A tavern favorite.
A basic copper blade. Not as strong as iron, but better than bare fists.
A spear made of bronze, combining copper and tin. Balanced and sharp.
A thick cloak made from rabbit fur. Warm and light, perfect for travelers.
A flowing robe made from fine linen. Cool and breathable, ideal for warm climates.
A durable vest crafted from deer pelt. Offers modest protection and warmth.
A delicately crafted candle infused with honey. Pleasantly aromatic and prized by nobles and clergy alike.
Fresh root and leaf vegetables, harvested from small garden plots.
Juicy, sun-ripened fruits picked straight from orchard trees.
Lean cuts from rabbits and birds caught in the wild.
Cleaned feathers used for arrows, bedding, or fletching.
Rough-hewn stone blocks ready for construction or carving.
Aromatic flower cones used to bitter and flavor ale.
A bundle of fragrant herbs gathered from meadows and woodland.
Washed and carded wool, ready for spinning or weaving.
A smoked sausage made from small game meat, perfect for long journeys.
A bundle of sharp arrows, fletched with feathers for accurate flight.
A heavy, woven cloak made from clean wool. Perfect for cold nights.
A simple tonic brewed from wild herbs. Used for minor wounds and fatigue.
A tightly packed bundle of fragrant herbs and hops, burned to calm the spirit.
